scene: Inferno XII — shattered descent, Minotaur and guarded boiling river
story: Dante and Virgil enter a landslide-like steep slope of broken rock leading down into the seventh circle.
The Minotaur rages at the travelers; Virgil invokes Theseus and the creature attacks itself in fury, allowing the pilgrims to descend.
Virgil comments on the ruined rock and its connection, within the poem, to the earthquake at Christ's descent into Hell.
A river of boiling blood, Phlegethon, contains violent souls submerged according to their offenses.
Armed centaurs patrol its banks and shoot at souls attempting to rise above their appointed depth.
Chiron recognizes that Dante is living because his movements disturb what he touches; Virgil requests safe passage.
Chiron assigns Nessus to guide them, and Nessus carries Dante across the blood at a shallower place.
The travelers arrive at the other bank; entry into the wood of suicides awaits the next intersection.
